card.problem_text:
Cook's membrane, case 1 (E = 1, ν = 1/3, compressible linear elasticity), SWG method.
Geometry: Tapered plate (Cook's membrane), 2D. The section gives no vertex coordinates; they are only in Figure 10.4. The only stated point is Q = (48, 52), the midpoint of the right (loaded) end.
Material: Linear elastic, compressible: E = 1, ν = 1/3. This is small-strain linear elasticity, not hyperelasticity. No units are given.
Boundary conditions: One end is clamped and the opposite end carries a shear traction. The text does not say which end is clamped (it is shown in Figure 10.4). The remaining edges are presumably traction-free, but the text does not say so.
Loading: Shear traction g = (0, 1/16) on the end opposite the clamp. The text does not say whether it is uniform.
Discretisation in the paper: SWG (stabilized weak Galerkin) scheme (2.15) on polygonal partitions: triangles, quadrilaterals, hexagons and octagons, with κ = 1 or κ = 0. For case 1 the only stated mesh is a quadrilateral partition with h = 1/16 (Fig. 10.7). Element and DOF counts for case 1 are not given. The refinement study (8,192 triangles, 12,416 DOF) is reported only for case 2.
Features: Corners where the clamped end meets the traction-free top and bottom edges of the tapered plate. These are clamped–free corners, so the elastic stress is singular there.; Corners where the loaded end meets the free edges. The traction jumps there, which may cause a weak stress concentration..
Question: which of these quantities can serve as trustworthy reference values: Vertical displacement at Q (Vertical displacement u2 at Q = (48, 52), the midpoint of the right end. The section reports it for comparison with [2, 22].); Displacement contour fields u1, u2 (Contour plots of the displacement components for κ = 1 and κ = 0 on a quadrilateral partition with h = 1/16. The κ = 0 and κ = 1 results are reported as very close.)?

spec.name: Cook's membrane, case 1 (E=1, ν=1/3, compressible small-strain linear elasticity), SWG scheme (2.15)
spec.geometry: 2D tapered plate (Cook's membrane). Vertex coordinates not given in the text (only in Fig. 10.4). The only stated point is Q = (48, 52), the midpoint of the right (loaded) end. One end is clamped and the opposite end is loaded; the top and bottom edges are presumably traction-free.
spec.material: Isotropic linear elastic, compressible: E = 1, ν = 1/3. No units. Small-strain linear elasticity, not hyperelasticity, so there is no material instability and no limit point. Plane strain vs. plane stress is not stated.
spec.loading: Shear traction g = (0, 1/16) on the end opposite the clamp. The text does not say whether it is uniform. The problem is linear, so there is no load-level dependence.
qois: Vertical displacement u2 at Q = (48, 52), the midpoint of the loaded end. This is a pointwise displacement far from the clamped–free corner singularities, so it should converge under refinement. It is a candidate reference value, but only if it is backed by a refinement study or matches literature values [2, 22] that themselves come from converged refinement. Case 1 reports only one mesh (quadrilateral, h = 1/16), so the paper alone does not establish convergence.

Displacement contour fields u1, u2 (κ = 1 and κ = 0, quadrilateral partition, h = 1/16). These are qualitative only. The fields are in H1 and converge globally, but the contour plots come from a single mesh and give no numerical values. The close agreement between κ = 0 and κ = 1 is a consistency check between stabilization variants, not evidence of convergence. They are not usable as quantitative reference values.
well_posedness: Dirichlet clamp on one end removes rigid-body modes, so the problem is well posed (Korn inequality). This assumes the clamp covers the whole end edge, which needs confirmation from Fig. 10.4.
The remaining top and bottom edges are assumed traction-free. This is not stated in the text.

Material stability: E = 1 > 0 and ν = 1/3 is well inside (-1, 0.5), so the material is strictly elliptic and compressible with no volumetric locking concern. Linear problem: no limit points, bifurcation or load-level dependence.

Singular features: the clamped end meets the free top and bottom edges at clamped–free corners, where the stress is singular. Pointwise peak stress near those corners will not converge. Energy, global displacement norms and displacements away from the corners (such as u2 at Q) will converge, possibly at a reduced global rate.

The loaded end meets the free edges at corners where the traction jumps (if the load is uniform). This gives a weak stress concentration near the corners next to Q. It affects pointwise stress there, but not displacement convergence at Q.
Convergence of any QoI needs a mesh refinement family. For case 1 the paper gives only one mesh (h = 1/16). The 8,192-triangle / 12,416-DOF refinement data is for case 2 only.
open_questions: Vertex coordinates of the membrane (only in Fig. 10.4). Is it the standard Cook geometry with (0,0), (48,44), (48,60), (0,44)?
Which end is clamped? Presumably the left end at x = 0, given Q on the right end, but the text does not say.
Is the shear traction g = (0, 1/16) uniform along the loaded end? With the standard end length of 16, this gives a total force of 1.
Are the top and bottom edges explicitly traction-free?
Numerical value of u2 at Q reported by the SWG scheme for case 1, and the literature values from [2, 22] it is compared with. These are not given in the provided text, so no number can be assumed.
Element and DOF counts for case 1, and whether any refinement sequence exists for case 1. Only h = 1/16 on quadrilaterals is stated.

Element mapping: SWG on polygonal partitions has no enum match. Q4 is chosen as the closest stand-in for the quadrilateral partition. The polynomial degree of the SWG interior and boundary spaces is not stated here.
Are triangle, hexagon and octagon partitions also used for case 1, and are their u2(Q) values reported? Agreement across element families would support the reference value.

assumptions: Geometry is the standard Cook's membrane (vertices (0,0), (48,44), (48,60), (0,44)), because the text gives coordinates only in Figure 10.4; Q = (48, 52) matches the midpoint of the right end of that geometry.
The left end x = 0 is clamped and the right end x = 48 is loaded, as in the standard benchmark. The text does not say which end is clamped, but Q is called the midpoint of the right (loaded) end.
The shear traction (0, 1/16) is taken as uniform along the loaded end, as in the standard benchmark. The text does not say whether it is uniform.
The top and bottom edges are traction-free. The text only says this is presumably so.
Plane strain is assumed because the text does not say whether the problem is plane strain or plane stress. This affects the value of v_Q, so any reference comparison has to use the same assumption.

Only v_Q is modeled as a point of interest. The displacement contour fields u1 and u2 are qualitative plots with no numbers in the text, so they cannot serve as quantitative reference values. At most they are a visual consistency check.

The clamped corners (0,0) and (0,44) are clamped–free corners where the stress is singular. The displacement at Q is still expected to converge under refinement, so it is a suitable verification quantity, but the point stresses at those corners are not.
